caribbean.title: Greater Antilles, west to east
caribbean.mnemonic: The big-island train: Cuba first, Jamaica tucked below, then Hispaniola split in reading order — Haiti left, Dominican right — with Puerto Rico trailing.

caribbean.title: The Lesser Antilles arc, north to south
caribbean.mnemonic: Kind Ants Dance Lightly, Very Gracefully, To Trinidad — the French islands fill the gaps, and Barbados stands apart, east into the open Atlantic.

pacific-islands.title: Melanesia: big to small, heading southeast
pacific-islands.mnemonic: The islands shrink as you sail southeast off Papua's tail — PNG, Solomons, Vanuatu, Fiji. Fiji is the hub where the Pacific's bands meet.

pacific-islands.title: Micronesia: dusted across the top, west to east
pacific-islands.mnemonic: Palau starts at the Philippines' doorstep, then Micronesia and the Marshalls; tiny Nauru hangs below, and Kiribati stretches on past the date line.

pacific-islands.title: Polynesia: the eastern three
pacific-islands.mnemonic: Northwest to southeast and shrinking in latitude: Tuvalu, Samoa, then Tonga below — the kingdom at the bottom of the triangle.

central-america.title: The isthmus, northwest to southeast
central-america.mnemonic: Guatemala leads with Belize on its Caribbean shoulder; then the split pair — El Salvador Pacific-side, Honduras Caribbean-side — and Nicaragua, Costa Rica, Panama single-file to Colombia.

northern-europe.title: The Baltic stack, top to bottom
northern-europe.mnemonic: Alphabetical from the top: Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania — E before L, and the two Ls in alphabetical order too.

south-america.title: The Guiana coast, west to east
south-america.mnemonic: Alphabetical sailing east: Guyana, then Suriname, then France's slice — English, Dutch, French, in the order the colonizers lined up.

sahel.title: The band, west to east
sahel.mnemonic: M, M, N along the desert's edge: the two M's first with the longer name westmost, then Niger — sitting directly on top of Nigeria — and Chad continuing the band beyond the region's edge.

western-africa.title: The coast, west to east
western-africa.mnemonic: Senegal wraps the Gambia, then the two Guineas (Bissau first), then the freed-slave pair Sierra Leone and Liberia; around the corner Ivory Coast and Ghana, the thin twins Togo and Benin, and Nigeria at the end. Cape Verde floats offshore.

central-asia.title: Kazakhstan on top, then west to east below
central-asia.mnemonic: One giant on top; below it, west to east: Turkmenistan on the Caspian, Uzbekistan in the middle touching everyone, then the mountain pair — Kyrgyzstan up, Tajikistan down.
